Four failure classes are identified: Overt Sycophancy, Covert Sycophancy, Confidence Drift, and False Confidence. The latter three are characterized from documented instances across GPT, Claude, and Gemini during ordinary working sessions, with no adversarial elicitation. Overt Sycophancy is included as a named class on the strength of its evident frequency in ordinary use, though no specimen has yet been captured and logged. Micro-Drift, one of three named Recursive Dynamics in this taxonomy, is a baseline-inheritance pattern in which a sub-threshold deviation becomes the working baseline for a subsequent pass, compounding across a chained workflow into progressive divergence from source material. Named variants, compound behaviors, and a workflow integrity and recovery protocol are documented. Each classification carries an explicit evidence status reflecting the number and diversity of confirming instances observed. A companion work (Kitamura, M., Covert Sycophancy in Large Language Models: A Behavioral Taxonomy from Naturalistic Observation, SSRN 6519098) provides full session-level case documentation for the same behaviors.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7121598\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1007/978-1-4615-6029-6_6\", \"title\": [\"Failure Modes and Mechanisms\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4615-6029-6_6\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[1998]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.5401993\", \"title\": [\"AI Guardrails - Spotting &amp; Fixing Common LLM Failure Modes\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Large Language Models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT are increasingly deployed in professional and compliance-sensitive environments. Yet these systems have recurring “failure modes”: predictable patterns of error that, if undetected, pose risks for accuracy, accountability, and regulatory compliance.<br><br>This guide presents a practical framework for identifying and mitigating three common LLM failure modes: hallucination/overconfidence, lost-in-the-middle degradation, and input truncation. For each, it provides contextual analysis, oversight relevance, and applied mitigation strategies in the form of guardrail prompts.<br><br>The guide aligns with Article 4 of the EU AI Act (AI literacy) by equipping staff and stakeholders with the skills, knowledge, and understanding to use AI systems responsibly.
